clue.text: Endeavour, with code, to follow script one rejigged

indicators.note: to follow means the code word comes after the rearranged letters
rejigged means rearranged, so the letters of script and one are put in a new order

parts.note: Morse code, the dots-and-dashes signalling system

explanation.surface: Someone tries to write code after reworking a script.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour looks like a common noun or verb, but it is the first name of Colin Dexter's detective, also the title of the prequel series.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour Morse is the given name of Colin Dexter's Oxford detective, so the name stands for the fictional policeman.

clue.text: Harboured new setter in the place we keep tools?

indicators.note: in places the setter's word inside the phrase for the place where we keep tools

parts.note: our shed: the shed belonging to us, where tools are kept
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A question about hiding a new compiler away in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is I, a crossword convention; 'the place we keep tools' must be read as 'our shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish a hope or grudge is to harbour it, keeping it alive in the mind.

clue.text: Fool's knocked up? You shouldn't have savoury food

indicators.note: knocked up in a down clue means the word for fool is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a sap is a fool; the 's is read as 'is' linking it
ta is a British informal thank-you, the polite reply to a gift

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for cooking a dish, told they need not have bothered with savoury food.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks, matching the gracious 'You shouldn't have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta dishes such as spaghetti or lasagne are typically savoury, so it is an example of savoury food.

clue.text: Keeper is cut and injured catching ball

indicators.note: catching means the rearranged letters hold the ball shape inside them
injured suggests damage, so the letters of is, cut and and are bent into new order

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is hurt and cut while catching the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeper reads as a football goalkeeper, but it means a guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a guardian or caretaker who keeps something safe, as in a museum keeper.

clue.text: Elliptical poet filled with love

indicators.note: filled with means the poet's name contains the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A poet whose writing is elliptical, brimming with love.
explanation.walkthrough: Elliptical suggests terse writing, but here it is the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, an oval or ellipse-like form.

clue.text: Where several films are shown many times

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cinema with several screens
second meaning: manifold, many times over

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the adjective meaning manifold, from Latin for many-folded.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiscreen cinema complex is called this, and the word also describes something having many parts or occurring in many forms.

clue.text: Picked up pen properly

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is entered as it sounds

explanation.surface: Someone lifted a pen correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up looks like lifting the pen; it signals hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something right means doing it correctly or in the proper way.

clue.text: One caught breaking into lodge is one who'll appeal

indicators.note: breaking into means these letters go inside the word for lodge

parts.note: to lodge a complaint is to enter it
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A burglar caught breaking into a lodge says something to appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lodge reads as a building to break into; here it is the verb to lodge, or enter, a document.
explanation.definitionFit: An enticer tempts or lures, so it is someone who holds appeal and draws people in.

clue.text: Decorative coating mostly fixed on condo's walls

indicators.note: on means the outer letters of condo sit after the shortened word for fixed
mostly means the word for fixed loses its last letter
walls are the outside letters of condo

parts.note: condo, the possessive being part of the surface

explanation.surface: Plaster was applied to the walls of a condominium.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat and ornament walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Unsuccessful Liz Taylor, gutted, curses periodically

indicators.note: gutted means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of Taylor
periodically means every other letter of curses is taken

explanation.surface: Elizabeth Taylor, devastated, swears now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was the UK's shortest-serving prime minister, in office for 49 days in 2022; Liz Taylor is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Liz Truss resigned after a few weeks as British prime minister, so she counts as the unsuccessful Liz.

clue.text: A red jumper, say, petite on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the word for petite wraps around the garment

parts.note: a jumper (British for sweater) is one example of a top

explanation.surface: A petite woman wearing a red jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a sweater in British English, an example of a top worn over the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal at red, which halts vehicles, is called this; red is the colour of that light.

clue.text: Marx banks a thousand pounds in big city

indicators.note: banks means the Marx brother's name lies on either side of the money

parts.note: Chico Marx, one of the Marx Brothers
G stands for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Karl Marx deposits a grand in a bank in a large city.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx suggests Karl but it is Chico, of the comedy Marx Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major US metropolis in Illinois, the third-largest American city.

clue.text: Edict is put out pertaining to religion

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbance, so the letters of edict and is are reordered

explanation.surface: A religious decree has been issued.
explanation.walkthrough: Put out reads as issuing the edict, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deistic relates to deism, belief in a creator who does not intervene, so it concerns religious faith.

clue.text: Further trouble that bishop's escaped

indicators.note: escaped means the bishop's letter leaves the word for trouble

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: More trouble arises because a bishop has run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional or more, as in 'one other thing', matching further.

clue.text: Patients changing doctors slip into tight flares

indicators.note: into means the word for slip goes inside the scrambled letters
tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of flares are scrambled

parts.note: to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: Someone trying to squeeze into tight-fitting flared trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight looks like describing the trousers; it is the anagram signal, drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Referrals are cases where a patient is passed from one doctor to another, usually a specialist.

clue.text: One won't transmit current abuse about American troops

indicators.note: about means the word for abuse goes round the American letter

parts.note: insult as a noun is verbal abuse
OR stands for other ranks, enlisted soldiers

explanation.surface: Present-day insults directed at American soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Current reads as present-day; it is electric current, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulator is a material that blocks the flow of electricity or heat.

clue.text: Factions litigate about one minor matter

indicators.note: about means the word for factions surrounds the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Rival groups go to court over something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary point, peripheral to the main question.

clue.text: Person digging melody catches Eleanor Rigby's intro

indicators.note: catches means the melody word holds the short name inside

parts.note: Nell is a pet form of Eleanor

indicators.note: intro means the opening letter of Rigby

explanation.surface: A song catching the opening of the Beatles' 'Eleanor Rigby'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleanor Rigby' is a Beatles song, which supports the melody picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunneller is someone who digs tunnels, an excavator underground.

clue.text: Elegant coats of Parisian evaluated differently

indicators.note: coats means the word for elegant wraps around the French word

explanation.surface: A stylish Parisian woman's coats.
explanation.walkthrough: Of Parisian means 'of' as a Parisian would say it, the French de.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to give it a new meaning or assess it in a new way.

clue.text: Identification for car drivers keeping sober in racing event

parts.note: reg is a British short form of a car's registration number

indicators.note: keeping means the drivers' organisation holds the sober letters

parts.note: the AA is the British Automobile Association, a motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Car registration lets drivers stay sober at a racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: Reg is the UK registration plate; the AA is Britain's motoring breakdown body.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting meeting with a series of boat or yacht races.

clue.text: Note individual's back on Twitter for a gas

indicators.note: on means the reversed part sits after the platform's letter
back means the note and individual are read in reverse order

parts.note: one is a single individual; the 's is the link

explanation.surface: Someone posts a note about a gas on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitter is now X, a modern twist on the single-letter trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a chemical element, a noble gas used in lamps.

clue.text: Observing unpopular leader of government

parts.note: not in means out of favour or unfashionable

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of government

explanation.surface: Watching an unpopular head of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means noticing or paying attention to something, as in observing details.

clue.text: Sort of flu soldier caught embracing drunken star

indicators.note: embracing means the soldier holds the drunken star inside
drunken signals the letters of star are jumbled

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A soldier with flu is caught hugging an intoxicated celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric flu is an informal name for gastroenteritis, a stomach bug.

clue.text: Vow to make black dresses wide

indicators.note: dresses means the word for make black clothes the letter for wide

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or blacken
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A promise to make black dresses roomier.
explanation.walkthrough: Dresses looks like garments; it is a verb, clothing the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, to take an oath.

clue.text: Measure of the weight of eg Ruby's vegetable, we hear

definitions.text: Measure of the weight of eg Ruby's

indicators.note: we hear means the answer sounds like the vegetable

explanation.walkthrough: Ruby reads as a woman's name; it is the gemstone.

clue.text: Superlatively silly goose could be here?

explanation.surface: A silly goose in a funny place.

clue.text: Ill-fated mission to Malaysia keeps heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means the letters read upwards
keeps means the letters are held within to Malaysia

parts.note: the letters run across the join of to and Malaysia

explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo was a Texas mission besieged in 1836, its defenders killed.

clue.text: Articles covering small, extinct ox in reference work

clue.text: Spent a pound, then nothing on the way back
